records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Multiple human absolute or relative bioavailability records for large peptidomimetic or macrocyclic agents are below 20%, including olcegepant <1%, dalfopristin <5%, docetaxel 8%, UK-427857 2.9%, almorexant 11.2%, methysergide 13%, and YH4808 10.1%, providing transferable low-F context for the query's large macrocyclic peptidomimetic structure.

The L4-related HCV protease inhibitor BMS-605339 has low aqueous solubility (7 µg/mL at pH 6.5) and its absorption may be limited by gastrointestinal efflux, supporting a low-absorption direction for this chemotype.

L5 gut-wall evidence shows related HCV protease inhibitors are P-gp/BCRP and/or CYP3A substrates; danoprevir has low passive permeability and its low human oral bioavailability is attributed to P-gp/MDR1 efflux, with Mdr1a/Bcrp knockout increasing oral AUC 4.7-fold and bioavailability 2.6-fold.

Grazoprevir is predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4/5 in the gastrointestinal tract, supporting intestinal first-pass loss in this chemotype; however, C64 notes intestinal P-gp may play a minimal role in grazoprevir absorption, so P-gp substrate status alone is not dispositive.

Retosiban human bioavailability of 17-25% is borderline and includes extensive first-pass elimination, and animal high-F records (retosiban rat ~100%, ER-30346 dog/rat 74/48%, UK-427857 dog ~40%, DORA-15 moderate) are species-specific and do not override human low measurements or the query's physicochemical barriers.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule is supplied.
No matched oral versus intravenous exposure data for the query are available.
No query-specific P-gp/BCRP/CYP3A substrate or intestinal metabolism measurement is supplied; L5 evidence is from other HCV protease inhibitors.
C64 indicates intestinal P-gp may play a minimal role in grazoprevir absorption, so the efflux mechanism may not be rate-limiting for every analog.
Animal high-F records are species-specific and not directly transferable to humans.
